passage:
Every spring, the town holds a plant market in front of the train station. People sell flowers, small trees, herbs, and vegetable plants.
This year, the market added a "plant doctor" table. Visitors could bring sick plants and ask for advice. A woman brought a yellowing tomato plant. A boy brought a cactus that had become soft.
The plant doctors explained that too much water can be as harmful as too little. They also showed people how to check soil and sunlight.
Many visitors came to buy plants, but they left with knowledge too.
The market became more than a place to shop. It became a place where people learned how to keep living things alive after taking them home.
